Sophie (support): @Evan thanks for the repro details. You said this started last night when your nightly embedding job ran, right? Can you paste the exact error lines you see?
Evan (CartoWave): Yep. Nightly job at ~02:10 UTC. Most of the run finished then spiked with 429s and a few "dimension mismatch" downstream failures. Here's the tail of the worker log: 
```
2026-03-14T02:12:05Z ERROR embed-worker: request failed status=429 body={\"error\":\"rate limit\"} attempt=12
2026-03-14T02:12:08Z WARN postprocess: embedding length mismatch expected=1536 got=0 id=rec_149
2026-03-14T02:12:09Z ERROR embed-worker: request failed status=429 body={\"error\":\"rate limit\"} attempt=13
```
Sophie (support): Got it. Are you batching client-side? What batch size and concurrency are you sending?
Evan (CartoWave): We chunk texts into batches of 256 and run 20 workers in parallel. Each worker posts one batch at a time. Overall concurrency ~20 requests/s. We also call the embeddings endpoint with model `open-embed-large-v2`.
Maria Gomez: Quick q — are those batches variable length? If some have empty strings we can get zero-length vectors (rare) but usually not dimension mismatch. Also, 1536 is a model-specific dim — consistent.
Evan (CartoWave): Batches are variable. Some items are short but not empty. We saw about ~0.3% of items flagged dimension=0.
Ajay Patel: I pulled the rate limiter logs for the customer's project id. We see a large burst from their API key at 02:11:55 — about 600 requests in 30s, then the global limiter started returning 429s. Headers indicate token-level quota reached then project-level burst cap kicked in.
InfraBot: alert: rate_limit.enforced project=cartowave-prod limit=burst_per_minute window=60s count=640 threshold=600
Sophie (support): Ah. So two problems: 1) burst/429s from concurrency; 2) some bad entries producing zero-length embeddings that blow up downstream. We should help them smooth the burst and add client-side validation.
Maria Gomez: For the burst: the platform exposes the `x-rw-limit-*` headers on responses. If the client sees `x-rw-rate-remaining: 0` or `Retry-After` it should back off. But customers often fire-and-forget many concurrent requests which overwhelms the burst cap. Recommend exponential backoff with jitter.
Evan (CartoWave): Is there a recommended client-side pattern? We're using bulk workers written in Go.
Maria Gomez: Example backoff pseudocode we recommend: 
```
base = 200ms
for attempt in 0..N:
  wait = base * 2^attempt + random(0, base)
  sleep(wait)
  retry_request()
```
Also throttle concurrency so max outstanding requests <= 10 for that model if using hosted plan.
Ajay Patel: I'll paste infra view of headers we returned during the spike: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
x-rw-rate-limit-type: burst
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 2026-03-14T02:12:58Z
```
Sophie (support): Evan — can you try a quick repro: run your job with concurrency=5 (workers) and batch_size=128 for a single run and share the logs? If you still see dimension=0 we can dig into payloads.
Evan (CartoWave): On it. I can repro locally. Quick dump: with concurrency=20 we hit 429s within 30s. With concurrency=5 it's steady. I did a run that produced a couple of zero-dim embeddings — raw input showed a line that was just `"\n"` which it's treating as empty after trimming. So we likely should filter out pure whitespace inputs.
Maria Gomez: Good find. That explains the zero dim. Suggest you run a pre-validation step to drop empty/whitespace-only texts. Also consider sending a few items per batch rather than giant 256-sized ones — big batches can momentarily cause sudden throughput bursts if many workers align.
Ajay Patel: Operational options for CartoWave: 
- Short term: implement client-side concurrency cap + backoff (recommended).
- Mid term: switch to Dedicated capacity so they get higher burst quotas and stable throughput.
- We can also whitelist specific API key to give elevated burst for a temporary window while they migrate. (Requires SOC approval.)
Sophie (support): Evan, want us to enable a temporary burst lift for the API key to let you catch up tonight? That would give you a 10m window with higher burst.
Evan (CartoWave): That would be great. We'll still change the job to pre-filter empty items and add backoff, just to be safe.
Maria Gomez: Also add metric collection: counts of 429s, requests/s, and a histogram of request sizes. Console -> Diagnostics -> Per-route shows these. We can set an alert for >10 429s/min.
Evan (CartoWave): One last question — we saw `dimension mismatch` errors at postprocess step. Is it safe to retry only the failed items or should we retry entire batch?
Maria Gomez: Retry per-item where possible. If you get a 429 for the batch, the safest path is to retry the whole batch after backoff. If you get a postprocess dimension mismatch for specific items (e.g., got dim=0), skip/blacklist the input and log it — often it's an input sanitation issue.
Sophie (support): Action items: 
- Evan: Add whitespace filter + reduce concurrency to 5-10, add backoff with jitter, lower batch to 64-128 for nightly run and rerun tonight.
- Ajay: Submit SOC ticket for temporary burst lift for key cartowave-prod (pending approval).
- Maria: Share a short runbook snippet to include in our KB about handling embedding 429s + dim mismatch.
Evan (CartoWave): Will do. Thanks everyone. Appreciated the quick turnaround. :pray:
Maria Gomez: I'll drop the runbook snippet here in a minute.
Maria Gomez: (adds runbook excerpt) — short checklist: 
1) Pre-validate: drop empty/whitespace texts.
2) Batch sizing: aim 32-128 per request for large corpora.
3) Concurrency: keep <=10 concurrent outstanding requests for hosted plans.
4) On 429: exponential backoff + jitter, respect `Retry-After`.
5) Telemetry: instrument 429s, latency, success per-item.
Sophie (support): Marking this resolved for now; will update if temporary lift is approved.
Evan (CartoWave): Confirmed — nightly job passed with the revised settings. No 429s after throttling. Thanks! :tada:
